key_insight: Combining histopathology AI, predicted morphological features, and manually assessed PRAME staining achieved high melanoma discrimination but little improvement over AI alone.
clinical_relevance: This diagnostic research—not drug discovery—offers a structured way to combine AI outputs with established pathology findings, without establishing readiness for clinical use.
method: Analyzed whole-slide images using the Virchow2 foundation model and STAMP framework.
Trained models to predict malignancy and established histopathological features.
Integrated AI scores and predicted features with manually assessed PRAME immunohistochemistry.
evidence_signal: In a retrospective cohort of 1,000 melanocytic lesions, models trained on 800 cases achieved test AUROCs of 0.970 for AI alone and 0.972 for the integrated model on 200 temporally held-out cases.
watch_item: The retrospective, PRAME-tested cohort and minimal discrimination gain warrant external and prospective validation before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Integrating Histopathology Foundation Models and PRAME Immunohistochemistry in Melanoma Diagnosis
